# `octo/redemption`

Add `octo/redemption` to the `Octo-Capabilities` header to receive these fields.

## Endpoints

This capability unlocks 6 endpoint(s).

- **`POST /redemption/credentials`**: Resolve Redemption Credentials. Body `RedemptionCredentialsRequest`.
- **`GET /redemption/lookup`**: Lookup.
  - **reference** (string, in query): Lookup by booking/ticket reference or redemption code.
  - **email** (string, in query): Lookup by email address.
  - **mobile** (string, in query): Lookup by mobile number.
- **`DELETE /redemption/noshow`**: No-show Route Variant. Body `RedemptionActionRequest`.
- **`POST /redemption/noshow`**: Mark No-show. Body `RedemptionActionRequest`.
- **`DELETE /redemption/redeem`**: Cancel Redemption (Unredeem). Body `RedemptionActionRequest`.
- **`POST /redemption/redeem`**: Redeem. Body `RedemptionActionRequest`.

## Integration notes

From [docs.ventrata.com/capabilities/redemption](https://docs.ventrata.com/capabilities/redemption).
All paths are public routes under `/octo`.

This capability is for **supplier and operator** connections: look up bookings and tickets, redeem
and unredeem them, and mark no-shows by redemption code.

### The response shape follows the request shape

The single rule that decides your return type:

> If `redemptionCode` is an array, the response is `array[Redemption Object]` **in input order**.
> Otherwise, the response is a single `Redemption Object`.

So a client must branch on what it sent, not on what it hopes to get. `GET /redemption/lookup`
always returns an array — one entry per match, and **a package product with redeemable inclusions
yields several**.

### Lookup takes one of three identifiers

`GET /redemption/lookup` needs at least one of `reference`, `email` or `mobile`. Each result carries
`redemptionCode`, `redeemable`, `unredeemableReason` and `unredeemableReasonCode` — check
`redeemable` before offering a scan, and surface `unredeemableReason` rather than a generic failure.

### Rejection returns 400 with two codes

When redemption is refused as not redeemable, the `400 BAD_REQUEST` body can carry **both**
`redemptionCode` and `redemptionErrorCode`. That is a second error code alongside the protocol-wide
`error` field, so read it for the specific reason.

### Every operation is reversible

- `POST /redemption/redeem` — redeem. `DELETE /redemption/redeem` — unredeem.
- `POST /redemption/noshow` — mark no-show; sets `status: "NO_SHOW"` and `utcNoshowedAt`.
- `DELETE /redemption/noshow` — documented as **wired to the same controller path** as
  `DELETE /redemption/redeem`, so its behaviour and response shape match unredeem.

Treat a scan as an undoable state change. `GET /redemption/lookup` is the authority on whether a
ticket was already used — never local state.

### Ticket-level resolution rewrites the object

When a redemption code resolves to a single ticket rather than a whole booking:

- `unitItems` is **reduced to that ticket only**,
- `voucher` is set to that ticket object,
- overlapping root fields are **overwritten with the ticket-level values**.

So the same schema means different things depending on what the code matched. A client that caches
the booking from a redemption response will hold a truncated copy — re-read with
`GET /bookings/{uuid}` if you need the whole booking.

Item units (`option.units[]` of type `OTHER`) additionally carry `scans: []`.

### One endpoint is unauthenticated

`POST /redemption/credentials` resolves an API key from lookup input and **requires no
authentication**: it picks the first key that can resolve the input. Useful for a scanning app that
does not yet know which supplier a code belongs to. Treat it as a discovery step, not a login.

### Cache the catalogue

Redemption responses reference product, option and unit metadata. The documentation recommends
caching it from `GET /products` rather than resolving per scan — scanning happens offline and under
time pressure.
